audit.whatIsWrong: The 2+ item row said K'Sante wins, while the prose directly under it (whys[6], spikes[3], phases[6].why, carry rating 10/10) says Nasus out-scales hard and you must close before then. The packet's level chart also gives the last stage to Nasus.
audit.why: The page rendered a stage whose verdict contradicted its own explanation. Nasus at 300 stacks with Fury of the Sands is the strongest late-game scaler in the lane and a 54.24% K'Sante win rate over 601 games comes from the early and item stages, not the late one.
audit.corrected: Flipped the 2+ items stage to Nasus in both layers as a matched pair (phases[6].side and win[6]), and rewrote phases[6].why so the row explains the flip instead of contradicting it. All other rows already agreed across layers and are untouched.

audit.why: Spike order is right: your level-3 full combo, level-6 All Out, Iceborn Gauntlet, then Nasus's late stack window. Nasus's own spikes are stack count and Fury of the Sands (120/100/80s), not an item timing, and the text already reflects that.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors carried from the same family the mirror audit already fixed on Nasus's page. (1) 'Q3 knock-up' — K'Sante's Ntofo Strikes slows and, at two stacks, PULLS enemies in; the knockback and stun are Path Maker (W). (2) whys[6] credits Wither with ignoring armour; Wither is a move and attack speed decay. The ability that beats stacked resistances is Fury of the Sands, which is percent-health.
audit.why: The mirror (nasus__ksante.json) recorded exactly this: 'Ntofo Strikes (Q) slows, and pulls only on its second stack. Path Maker (W) is the knockback and stun.' Restating the same mechanics from K'Sante's side keeps the two directions consistent, and the flagged missing interaction 'resistances-invalidated' points at R, not W.
audit.corrected: Q at two stacks pulls Nasus in; Path Maker (W) is the knockback and stun and deals true damage; All Out (R) is what launches him through a wall. Nasus's armour-invalidating tool is Fury of the Sands' percent-health damage, and Wither (15/14/13/12/11s, 700 range) is a move and attack-speed decay.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: no concrete cooldown sequencing anywhere (sequencingCues 0). dosFull[0].d said only 'Only engage once it is down or baited'.
audit.why: Wither's real cooldown makes the advice actionable.
audit.corrected: Wither is 15s at rank 1 and costs 80 mana at 700 range — bait it, then commit inside that window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warned that Siphoning Strike is an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: Flagged missing interaction 'autoreset-burst-tell': his damage arrives on the attack wind-up, not on a visible cast, so the step-back cue is earlier than players expect.
audit.corrected: Noted in the audit; not written to the page because no existing field could carry it inside the length band without dropping a verified fact already there.

edits.after: He out-scales hard: Wither guts your attack and move speed while Fury of the Sands burns percent health — armour alone does not answer that.

edits.before: Your full Q-W combo is online — W into a Q-stacking Nasus, then Q3 knock-up to deny stacks and chunk him before he has Wither.

edits.before: Nasus is helpless at Level 1-2 — he has no stacks, no Wither until later, and just wants to last-hit with Q. Don't let him free-farm: at Level 3 you have the full Q-W combo, so W a Nasus who walks up to stack, then Q3 to knock him up and deny those last-hits. Every stack you deny is permanent damage off his late game, so trade hard and shove him off the wave while his only answer is to soak Wither-less.
edits.after: Nasus is helpless at Level 1-2 — he has no stacks, no Wither until later, and just wants to last-hit with Q. Don't let him free-farm: at Level 3 you have the full combo, so Path Maker (W) knocks back and stuns a Nasus who steps up to stack, and two Q hits pull him back in. Every stack you deny is permanent damage off his late game, so trade hard while Wither is still a 15s cooldown.
